claim: Six human HIV-specific ADCC antibodies were isolated from a sample collected 914 days post-infection from a clade A-infected Kenyan woman.
source: We previously reported the isolation of six monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), each with potent antibody-dependent cell cytotoxicity (ADCC) activity, from a sample collected 914 days post-infection (D914) from a clade A-infected Kenyan woman (Williams et al., 2015; Williams et al., 2019).

claim: Four of the six ADCC antibodies target two distinct gp41 Env epitopes.
source: All these mAbs derived from distinct B cell lineages, with four targeting two distinct gp41 Env epitopes (006, 016, 067, 072), and the other two targeting distinct gp120 Env epitopes (105, 157).
evidence: The text explicitly states the epitope targets for the six antibodies.

claim: Two of the six ADCC antibodies target distinct gp120 Env epitopes.

claim: One of the gp120 targeting mAbs (105) had modest capacity to neutralize cell-free virus.

claim: Full-length antibody variable region genes were sequenced from five longitudinal blood samples spanning from pre-infection to over 4 years post-infection.

evidence: The text describes the sequencing approach and timepoints used.

claim: Sequencing libraries ranged in sample coverage between 6 and 409% with an average of 100% coverage based on estimated B cell frequencies.
source: Amongst the different antibody chains and timepoints sequenced, the sequencing libraries ranged widely in their sample coverage, between 6 and 409% with an average of 100% coverage, based on estimated B cell frequencies within the available peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) samples (Table 1).
evidence: The text provides specific coverage statistics, referencing Table 1 for detailed data.

claim: Each 10 mL PBMC sample represents only ~0.22% of the subject's whole-body circulating blood volume.
source: This is for two reasons: (1) each 10 mL PBMC sample is only ~0.22% of the subject's whole-body circulating blood volume (~4.5 L), not counting lymphoid organs or peripheral tissue and (2) circulating human memory B cell repertoires fluctuate over time (Horns et al., 2019; Laserson et al., 2014), making it difficult to accurately track clonal B cell families.
evidence: The text provides a calculation of sample representation relative to total blood volume.
